title.narrative: Provision of integrated recovery and resilience building services to most vulnerable communities in Dar’a and Al-Hasakeh.

description.narrative: ltpgtUnder this action, NRC Syria Country Office (SCO) is proposing a comprehensive 12-month project that aims at addressing the critical needs of the crisis- and displacement-affected population in Dar’a and Al-Hasakeh Governorates. Throughout this initiative, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene “WASH”, Shelter, and Livelihoods and Food Security (LFS) essential basic services, recovery and resilience support will be delivered to 24,894 people in need of the most vulnerable communities in both governorates especially focusing on underserved areas with high severity scale (S.S), through intersectoral integrated approach designed to meet the specific needs in each location as identified by NRC’s needs assessment and observed on the ground. The proposed integration between the different core competencies will demonstrate a greater impact on the population, while safe and inclusive programming (SIP) aspects will be mainstreamed throughout all the interventionsltbrgtUnder the WASH outcome, life-sustaining interventions will be prioritized in areas with minimal access to safe water. The NRC project will deliver essential WASH services to vulnerable communities in both Governorates, targeting 24,506 project participants with improved access to safe water and reliable water resources. This will include the rehabilitation of the water systems in Shikh Sa’ad community, Nawa sub-district in Izra’ district in Dar’a targeting 12,500 people in need, and six water systems in Jawadiyah and Qahtaniyyeh sub-districts in Al-Hasakeh targeting 12,006 others. Along with the rehabilitation of water systems, NRC will ensure full functionality of elevated tanks and consequently the entire water system, by conducting the needed rehabilitation work for non-functional ones.ltbrgtUnder the Shelter outcome, NRC intervention focuses on addressing the immediate needs of and improving shelter conditions for displacement-affected population in two collective shelters in Al-Hasakeh city. These shelters currently have very poor conditions, NRC will rehabilitate the shelters to ensure protection from weather conditions and meeting safety standards for around 388 dwellers, including the elderly and people with disabilities (PWDs), which is crucial in overcrowded shelters like those in Al-Hasakeh city. ltbrgtUnder the FSA outcome, this project will target 720 (405 female, 315 male) participants who are the most vulnerable segment of the population. In Sheikh Saed – Nawa sub-district area of Dar’a Governorate, particularly female-headed households (FHHs), through income-generating activities (IGA) support. NRC will provide livelihoods support to 90 FHHs in the form of technical training and cash grants to start their own income-generating activities for their food and income self-sufficiency. In addition, NRC will provide assistance to farmers households who have recently returned to their place of origin. The assistance package will include supporting 72 farmers with agriculture inputs grants and training. ltbrgtNRC will ensure community engagement and conduct capacity-building initiatives to local committees. Regular community meetings will promote transparency and foster stakeholder ownership. A comprehensive monitoring and evaluation framework will assess project impact and guide necessary adjustments. Sustainability measures include ongoing training for local maintenance teams, formal handover of rehabilitated facilities to local authorities, and community-led monitoring. Follow-up support and technical assistance post-project will also be provided. This approach aims to enhance community resilience, reduce dependency on external aid, and create a lasting positive impact.ltbrgtlt/pgt
